scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A laser printer prints a full page in seconds, and the paper comes out warm. Why warm? And where's the laser?

scenes.name: charge
scenes.text: Inside is a rotating drum with a special coating. First, it's given an even electric charge all over.

scenes.name: laser
scenes.text: A laser, bounced off a spinning mirror, sweeps across the drum. Wherever it hits, the charge changes, drawing your page invisibly.

scenes.name: toner
scenes.text: Toner is a super fine powder, also charged. It sticks only to the spots the laser drew, so the drum now carries your text.

scenes.name: transfer
scenes.text: The paper gets a charge too, strong enough to pull the toner off the drum and onto the page.

scenes.name: fuse
scenes.text: Then hot rollers melt the toner and press it into the paper. That's why pages come out warm.

scenes.name: vsink
scenes.text: Inkjets spray tiny drops of liquid ink instead. Laser printers are usually faster and cheaper per page for lots of text.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Charge, laser, toner, heat. A page in seconds. Follow for more on how things really work.
